description:
Pattern observed at:
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:982-984
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs:1335-1337
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/identity.rs:423-425
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/submission.rs:574-576
- (and probably sieve.rs, vacation.rs)
- crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/card.rs:281-283 (post JMAP-qz9v.52)
- crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/addressbook.rs:361-363 (post JMAP-qz9v.52)
- likely chat-server, calendars-server, tasks-server, filenode-server siblings

JMAP-qz9v.52 originally recommended replacing the silent 'continue' on an
unreachable-validated path with .expect("validated above as string") so the
unreachable case panics audibly rather than skipping silently. That change
was deferred for the bead's contacts-server-specific scope because every
canonical sibling currently uses the let-else-continue pattern; applying
.expect() to contacts-server alone would create cross-crate divergence.

The right scope is a workspace-canonical sweep: change mail-server's
sites first (it's the canonical extension-server template), then propagate
to every extension-server sibling in the same pass.

Mechanical work — find each 'let Some(...) = ... else { continue; // unreachable: validated above };'
pattern and convert to '.expect("validated above as ...")' so the
invariant break panics with a useful message instead of skipping the entry
and producing a misleading /set response.

Engineering case for the change: the comment 'unreachable: validated above'
admits the path is dead. A skip on a dead-path means a future refactor that
moves or removes the validator would silently lose data; an .expect() would
fail loudly at the regression point. The let-else pattern is one of the
workspace AGENTS.md 'silent-truncation/silent-drop in any function that
mutates state is a data-integrity bug class' family (bd:JMAP-wlip.1).
title: Workspace sweep: replace 'let Some(s) = ... else { continue; // unreachable: validated above }' with .expect() audibility
